terms.plain: One system that stores every kind of company data and lets you query it like a database.
terms.why: One copy of data serves both reports and experiments, so nobody keeps duplicating it.
terms.quote: A data lakehouse is a modern data management architecture that combines the advantages of data lakes and data warehouses.

terms.plain: A cheap store holding files of any type, with no rules or quality checks.
terms.why: Cheap to keep everything, but slow and risky to report from on its own.
terms.quote: While a data lake stores structured and unstructured data at scale, a data lakehouse, such as IOMETE, goes a step further by incorporating data warehouse features.

terms.plain: A tidy database built for fast business reporting, fed by copied and cleaned data.
terms.why: Buyers already have one, so explain how the lakehouse replaces or feeds it.
terms.quote: It brings together the scalability of data lakes with the reliability, data quality, ACID transactions, and security features of data warehouses.

terms.plain: The free file format that makes ordinary storage behave like a reliable table.
terms.why: Your data stays readable by many tools, not just this one.
terms.quote: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets.

terms.plain: The free engine that does the heavy calculating when someone runs a big query.
terms.why: It is the horsepower behind every query and job on the platform.
terms.quote: IOMETE utilizes Apache Spark, a widely adopted open-source data processing engine, known for its speed and versatility.

terms.plain: Software that runs and restarts applications across a fleet of ordinary servers.
terms.why: It means the platform rides on standard servers the buyer already knows how to run.
terms.quote: IOMETE runs on Kubernetes (any cloud provider or on-premises data center), stores data in object storage, and keeps metadata in PostgreSQL .

terms.plain: The principle that a country's or company's rules decide where data lives and who may touch it.
terms.why: Regulators and security teams approve only vendors who cannot move data abroad.
terms.quote: The platform operates entirely within your infrastructure, ensuring that no data is sent outside of your organization.

terms.plain: The legal duty to keep data physically inside a chosen country or region.
terms.why: A deal dies if the buyer's regulator forbids data crossing borders.
terms.quote: This policy will help maintain data privacy and comply with country-specific regulations.

terms.plain: A network with no internet connection at all, used where security is extreme.
terms.why: Only software that installs fully offline sells into defence, banks and hospitals.
terms.quote: It runs on your own Kubernetes, on-premises, in your cloud account or air-gapped.

terms.plain: Software installed on servers the customer owns, usually in their own building.
terms.why: Buyers keep full control and reuse hardware they already paid for.
terms.quote: It offers flexibility and can be deployed anywhere – on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid environment.

terms.plain: You run the software on your own machines instead of renting it from a vendor.
terms.why: No third party holds the data, which is often the deciding factor.
terms.quote: IOMETE is a self-hosted data lakehouse: SQL, Spark jobs, streaming and notebooks on Apache Iceberg.

terms.plain: Some systems sit in a company data centre, others in a cloud provider.
terms.why: Most large buyers are already mixed and need one view across both.
terms.quote: IOMETE is a hybrid (cloud & on-premises) platform that allows users to store, manage, and analyze large amounts of data.

terms.plain: Being trapped with one supplier because moving your data out is too painful.
terms.why: Buyers fear it, and open files they can read elsewhere remove that fear.
terms.quote: Arrow Flight clients and external engines that use the IOMETE Iceberg REST catalog also read data straight from storage, so the endpoint must be reachable from their networks too.

terms.plain: A published, royalty-free way to lay out table files that any tool can read.
terms.why: Different tools and clouds read the same files, so the buyer stays free.
terms.quote: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets.

terms.plain: The rules that decide how a table's files are named, arranged and updated.
terms.why: It is the difference between tidy tables and a folder of loose files.
terms.quote: Incremental models are supported on Iceberg tables, the platform's default table format.

terms.plain: The index that records which tables exist and where their files are kept.
terms.why: Without it, tools cannot find the data or agree on what a table is.
terms.quote: A Spark Catalog is a component in Apache Spark that manages metadata for tables and databases within a Spark session.

terms.plain: The shared bookkeeping service that remembers table names, columns and locations.
terms.why: Every tool relies on it, so losing it means losing the map to your data.
terms.quote: Data Lake Metadata: Specifically tailored for the Hive Metastore and Iceberg Metastore, this involves detailed metadata regarding data lake databases, tables, partitions, columns, and more.

terms.plain: The management layer that runs the console, settings and scheduling.
terms.why: Management can sit in one place while the actual data stays in another.
terms.quote: IOMETE Enterprise Edition offers a control plane and multi-data plane architecture.

terms.plain: The part that stores and processes data, running inside the customer's own network.
terms.why: It can live in the buyer's region while management runs elsewhere.
terms.quote: IOMETE Data Plane : This is the infrastructure component that handles the processing and movement of data within the IOMETE ecosystem.

terms.plain: Changes either fully succeed or fully fail, so numbers never end up half-written.
terms.why: Finance can trust the reports, which raw file dumps cannot offer.
terms.quote: This means you can perform operations like ACID transactions, updates, deletes, and merges within your data lakehouse environment.

terms.plain: Ask the data what it looked like last Tuesday and get exactly that answer.
terms.why: Audits and arguments about changed reports get settled in minutes.
terms.quote: Apache Iceberg provides versioning and time travel capabilities, allowing users to query data as it existed at a specific point in time.

terms.plain: A saved picture of the whole table after each change.
terms.why: Every change is recoverable and old versions can be restored quickly.
terms.quote: Each write to an Iceberg table creates a new snapshot , or version, of a table.

terms.plain: Housekeeping that merges thousands of tiny files into a few bigger ones.
terms.why: Without it, queries slow down month by month and storage costs creep up.
terms.quote: Table compaction plays a vital role in optimizing performance by consolidating smaller data files into larger ones, which reduces overhead and enhances query efficiency.

terms.plain: An update rewrites whole files, so reads stay fast and writes cost more.
terms.why: Good for tables read constantly and changed rarely.
terms.quote: This document focuses on the behavior of table compaction operations for Copy-on-Write (COW) and Merge-on-Read (MOR) tables.

terms.plain: Updates are stored as small notes and applied the moment someone reads.
terms.why: Writes stay cheap and quick, at the cost of slightly slower reads.
terms.quote: With merge-on-read, format v3 tables store deletes as compact deletion vectors (Puffin files) instead of rewriting data files.

terms.plain: Splitting a huge table into labelled chunks so queries skip what they do not need.
terms.why: Queries return in seconds instead of scanning everything you own.
terms.quote: Features like hidden partitioning and metadata pruning keep query planning efficient regardless of table size.

terms.plain: Physically sorting big tables on the columns people filter by, so most files are skipped.
terms.why: It is the tuning knob that rescues slow dashboards without buying more servers.
terms.quote: Data files in manifests are sorted by fields in the partition spec.

terms.plain: A three-step habit: keep raw copies, then cleaned data, then business-ready tables.
terms.why: It is the standard way teams organise a warehouse, so naming it sounds fluent.
terms.quote: dbt is an open-source tool for writing SQL models, testing them, and deploying them like any other software project.

terms.plain: Copying and cleaning data from source systems into a place you can analyse it.
terms.why: It is most of a data team's workload, and most of its pain.
terms.quote: Query Federation Engine : Seamlessly query data from multiple sources, including relational and NoSQL databases, and flat files without the need for complex ETL pipelines.

terms.plain: Load the raw data first, then clean it in place using SQL.
terms.why: It is how modern cloud teams work, and SQL skills already exist in-house.
terms.quote: If your team already runs analytics with version control, tests, and CI, dbt fits the same workflow for SQL transformations.

terms.plain: A live feed of every insert, update and delete happening in a source system.
terms.why: Keeps the warehouse current without nightly full reloads of everything.
terms.quote: Replicates CDC events from MySQL and PostgreSQL to Iceberg tables using Debezium Server.

terms.plain: Getting data into the platform from wherever it is created.
terms.why: Nothing can be analysed until it lands here, so it is the first project.
terms.quote: Event Streams ingest events over HTTP and write them to Apache Iceberg tables in near real time.

terms.plain: You can add or rename columns without breaking reports or rewriting old files.
terms.why: Source systems change constantly, and nobody wants a rebuild each time.
terms.quote: Schema evolution supports add, drop, update, or rename, and has no side-effects

terms.plain: The query sends its filters down to the source so only matching rows travel back.
terms.why: Far less data crosses the network, so answers arrive much sooner.
terms.quote: The option to enable or disable predicate push-down into the JDBC data source.

terms.plain: The program that actually does the calculating when a query runs.
terms.why: It sets the speed ceiling, which is what buyers benchmark.
terms.quote: Spark is the execution engine behind every query and job in IOMETE.

terms.plain: The scheduler deciding which data jobs run, when, and in what order.
terms.why: Overnight failures are usually scheduling problems, not data problems.
terms.quote: Jobs are submitted only when cluster capacity is available , reducing the chances of failure due to insufficient compute resources.

terms.plain: A diagram of tasks showing which step must finish before the next can start.
terms.why: It is how engineers describe dependencies, and it maps to the business process.
terms.quote: Airflow can render job_id and config_override from parameters supplied when you trigger a DAG.

terms.plain: A short trial on your own data, proving the software works before you buy.
terms.why: Buyers want proof, not slides, and a two-week trial usually decides the deal.
terms.quote: Demos and POCs - Quick setup for evaluations

terms.plain: The full cost of running something for years, not just the purchase price.
terms.why: Finance compares options on this, and storage bills usually dominate.
terms.quote: Spending wisely on those resources takes more thought.

terms.plain: The standard language for asking questions of data held in tables.
terms.why: Every analyst and dashboard tool already speaks it, so nobody retrains.
terms.quote: Lakehouse Platform : Powered by Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg, it offers a robust SQL interface for data exploration and analytics, including ACID-compliant operations, schema evolution, and data versioning.

terms.plain: The dashboard software analysts already use, such as Power BI or Tableau.
terms.why: Buyers keep their existing dashboards instead of relearning a new tool.
terms.quote: BI Tool Integration : Effortlessly work with major BI tools for comprehensive business intelligence experiences.

terms.plain: A fast pipe that moves query results to dashboards without slow conversion.
terms.why: Big extracts land in dashboards in seconds rather than minutes.
terms.quote: Arrow Flight (port 33333): high-performance gRPC data transfer (when enabled)

terms.plain: Storage that speaks the same protocol as Amazon's S3, from any vendor.
terms.why: The buyer can reuse existing storage instead of buying a new silo.
terms.quote: Object storage: Apache Ozone, Dell ECS, IBM Cloud Object Storage, MinIO or any other S3-compatible storage, AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.

terms.plain: Cheap, almost unlimited file storage that keeps data as whole objects.
terms.why: It is where nearly all the cost sits, so it drives the price conversation.
terms.quote: Object Storage : A durable and available object storage system, with Apache Ozone configured for optimal performance.

terms.plain: A named area on the servers where one team's work runs, with its own limits.
terms.why: Teams get their own space and budget without building separate systems.
terms.quote: A namespace quota caps how much CPU, memory, storage, and how many pods the workloads in one Kubernetes namespace can use.

terms.plain: Permissions attached to job roles, so people see only what their role allows.
terms.why: Access reviews and audits become a list lookup rather than guesswork.
terms.quote: They seamlessly integrate with existing data security rules to enforce role-based access control (RBAC).

terms.plain: Sensitive fields like card numbers show as XXXX to staff who do not need them.
terms.why: Analysts can work on real data without ever seeing private details.
terms.quote: With this feature, you can create policies that mask or anonymize specific columns containing sensitive data, such as PII , PCI , and PHI , dynamically in the query output.

terms.plain: Rules that hide certain rows, so a German team only sees German customers.
terms.why: One shared table can serve many countries without breaking local law.
terms.quote: IOMETE Row-level Filter policies allow users to access only a subset of data based on the context in which they interact with the data.

terms.plain: One company login that gets a person into every approved tool.
terms.why: Security teams refuse anything that creates yet another password.
terms.quote: Single sign-on enables you to authenticate your users using your organization’s identity provider.

terms.plain: An agreed way for a company login system to vouch for who a user is.
terms.why: It is the checkbox that gets past enterprise security review.
terms.quote: SSO supports using either SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC) .

terms.plain: A newer login standard where one company account signs you into many tools.
terms.why: Most modern identity providers prefer it over the older standard.
terms.quote: With OpenID Connect (OIDC) single sign-on, users sign in to IOMETE with their account at your identity provider (IdP), such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google, or Keycloak.

terms.plain: Automatically creates and removes accounts when the HR system changes.
terms.why: Joiners and leavers are handled without tickets, which auditors like.
terms.quote: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is a standard for automating the exchange of user identity information between identity domains, or IT systems.

terms.plain: An independent audit report proving a supplier protects customer data properly.
terms.why: Security teams will not sign a contract without seeing it.
terms.quote: Recommended, especially for audit or compliance requirements.

terms.plain: European rules forcing financial firms to prove their systems survive disruption.
terms.why: Banks must document supplier resilience, so evidence wins the deal.
terms.quote: Checks run every 10 seconds, the service retains 48 hours of history, and status changes push to the console in real time.

terms.plain: European law setting safety and transparency duties for AI systems.
terms.why: Buyers building AI need to show where training data lived and who could see it.
terms.quote: IOMETE is a state-of-the-art, fast, scalable, user-friendly Data Lakehouse Platform for AI and Analytics .

terms.plain: European law controlling how personal data may be stored, shared and deleted.
terms.why: Fines are large enough that privacy rules can stop a purchase.
terms.quote: This approval workflow keeps sensitive labels like PII or GDPR consistent across your catalog.

terms.plain: Any detail that can identify a real person, such as a name, email or ID number.
terms.why: It is the data regulators care about, so it needs hiding by default.
terms.quote: Personally identifiable information such as email, phone number, name, or address.

terms.plain: How long someone waits between asking a question and seeing the answer.
terms.why: Slow dashboards are the complaint that starts most replacement projects.
terms.quote: Views that perform heavy transformations, or stack on top of other views, are slow to query.

terms.plain: How much data the system can move or process in a given period.
terms.why: It decides whether a nightly load finishes before the business day starts.
terms.quote: Pick driver and executor instance types that fit your throughput.

terms.plain: A written promise about reliability, speed and support response times.
terms.why: Operations teams are measured against it, so they ask every supplier.
terms.quote: This feature is invaluable for disaster recovery, high availability, and multi-region deployments.

terms.plain: A preset machine size, small or large, chosen for each piece of work.
terms.why: It is the dial that trades cost against speed on every workload.
terms.quote: A node type is a reusable template that defines CPU (in millicores) and memory (in MiB) for a Spark driver or executor.

terms.plain: The machines that crunch the numbers in parallel, plus the one in charge.
terms.why: More of them means faster jobs, and a bigger monthly bill.
terms.quote: Everything in IOMETE runs on Kubernetes, so the simplest way to add capacity is to add worker nodes.

terms.plain: A scheduled program that processes a large amount of data on its own.
terms.why: It is the nightly plumbing that fills the tables everyone reports on.
terms.quote: Each Spark Job runs as an isolated Spark application with its own driver and (optionally) executors.

terms.plain: A one-off question typed by a person and answered in seconds.
terms.why: This is the experience most buyers actually judge the platform on.
terms.quote: Since storage and compute are decoupled, you can size each cluster for its workload (batch ETL, interactive analytics, a dedicated BI connection) and shut it down when it's idle to stop accruing costs.

terms.plain: A pool of rented computing power that answers queries and then can be switched off.
terms.why: Shutting it off when idle is the easiest way to cut the bill.
terms.quote: A compute cluster gives you dedicated CPU and memory, powered by Apache Spark, for running queries.

terms.plain: The rules and records that keep data trustworthy, permitted and traceable.
terms.why: Regulated buyers cannot buy a platform that ignores it.
terms.quote: Data Governance : Spark Catalogs , Data Security policies, and Audit logs.

terms.plain: Letting each business team own and publish its own data for others to use.
terms.why: Large firms reorganising around teams use this language, so match it.
terms.quote: Multi-Domain Support : Logical separation of teams, projects, or environments into domains, each with independent resources, members, and roles.

terms.plain: A ready-to-use dataset one team publishes for others to consume.
terms.why: It turns data into something with an owner, a promise and a user.
terms.quote:
VIEW_DATA_PRODUCT 
View data products. 

MANAGE_DATA_PRODUCT 
Create and manage data products.

terms.plain: A shared dictionary of business terms so every report defines revenue the same way.
terms.why: It ends the meeting where three dashboards show three different numbers.
terms.quote: Publish your report to the Power BI Service and open its semantic model's settings.

terms.plain: Ask one question across several separate systems without copying them together first.
terms.why: It skips months of integration work and answers questions this week.
terms.quote: Query Federation Engine : Seamlessly query data from multiple sources, including relational and NoSQL databases, and flat files without the need for complex ETL pipelines.

terms.plain: Software whose code is public, free to use and changeable by anyone.
terms.why: No licence fees and no single supplier controlling the roadmap.
terms.quote: Apache Ozone is an open-source (Apache License 2.0) distributed object store with an S3-compatible API.

terms.plain: Data handled continuously as it arrives, rather than in nightly batches.
terms.why: Fraud alerts and live pricing only work if the data is fresh.
terms.quote: Real-time data ingestion endpoints powered by Papyrus, a Rust-based ingestion engine.

terms.plain: A searchable list of every table, with descriptions, owners and tags.
terms.why: Analysts stop asking where the data is, which saves weeks of work.
terms.quote: Instead of hunting through individual catalogs, the Data Catalog lets you search, browse, and tag every table from one place.

terms.plain: Adding machines automatically when work spikes, and removing them afterwards.
terms.why: It stops the buyer paying for idle servers all weekend.
terms.quote: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) lets individual services scale their replica count based on CPU or memory utilization.

terms.plain: The standard plug that lets dashboards and tools talk to a database.
terms.why: If it is missing, the buyer's favourite tool simply cannot connect.
terms.quote: HiveServer2 (port 10000): JDBC /ODBC connections from BI tools, dbt , and other SQL clients
